one_liner: A 46-year-old man with a history of prior microdiskectomy presents with 4 months of right-sided low back and right leg pain, found to have an acute right S1 radiculopathy and scheduled for follow-up.

course.narrative: A 46-year-old gentleman presented with a four-month history of gradual onset right-sided low back pain radiating to the right leg and ankle, worsened by activity and accompanied by occasional subtle right leg weakness. Physical exam showed positive straight leg raising on the right and absent ankle reflexes. Lumbar MRI revealed a right paracentral disc at L5-S1 encroaching upon the right exiting S1 nerve root. A needle EMG was performed and showed spontaneous activity and chronic denervation in right-sided muscles, confirming an acute right S1 radiculopathy. The results were discussed with the patient.
